subject: Observability dry-run: edge forwarder -> SIEM ingestion and trace hooks
messages:
From: Sarah Wojcik <sarah@acmecloud.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: LogOps Team <logops@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability dry-run: edge forwarder -> SIEM ingestion and trace hooks

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for agreeing to do the observability dry-run this week. We're planning a small-scale exercise to validate the forwarder configuration, firewall/egress rules, and tracehook correlation before our broader rollout. High-level asks: 

- Confirm a recommended forwarder config (Syslog/HEC/Splunk HEC) and a minimal TLS setup for the private forwarder.
- Provide a short tracehook snippet we can install into our app sidecar to emit the correlation ID to spans.
- Walk through the network requirements (egress IPs, ports, and proxy auth) so our infra team can open the right rules.

Proposed window: Thu 25 Apr 2029 14:00-16:00 PDT. Let us know if that slot works. I've attached an internal checklist from our LogOps team showing what we'll attempt in the run.

Props: attached dryrun-checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Wojcik
Observability Lead, AcmeCloud

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wojcik <sarah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability dry-run: edge forwarder -> SIEM ingestion and trace hooks

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Thu 25 Apr 14:00 PDT works for us; I'll book a 90-minute slot and include a short runbook review at the top. Quick responses to your bullets: 

- Forwarder: we recommend the forwarder-config-example.yaml I attached (TLS to HEC, client certs optional for this first dry-run). Use HEC token auth for the ingestion endpoint; that keeps things simple for the run.
- Tracehook snippet: attaching a minimal tracehook-snippet.txt with the example header propagation you can drop into your sidecar. It emits x-redwood-correlation-id and maps it to the span_id.
- Network: we need TCP 443 outbound to: 34.120.45.9 (primary ingest), 34.120.46.10 (fallback). If you sit behind a corporate proxy please ensure CONNECT to these hosts is allowed and that the proxy presents an allowlist for the HEC token.

Prep items for your LogOps team: cert chain if you plan mTLS; there is a no-mTLS path for the dry-run using HEC token. We'll do a smoke verify (small batch logs + one trace) then scale to 5 concurrent clients.

I'll bring Kimberly to cover data scrub/mapping and Hiro for networking nuances. Attached: forwarder-config-example.yaml, tracehook-snippet.txt

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wojcik <sarah@acmecloud.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Apr 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability dry-run: edge forwarder -> SIEM ingestion and trace hooks

Thanks — two technical notes from my side before the run: 

1) Mapping & scrubbing: please confirm which fields we should drop or hash pre-ingest. For the dry run leave PII in place but flag it so we can exercise the scrubbing rule later. Example: customer_email => hash; vm_private_ip => drop.

2) HEC batch sizing: We'll push a small sample (batch_size=50 events) to validate ingestion latency. If you have a synthetic generator please set event interval=200ms.

3) Trace correlation: the tracehook snippet is fine, but make sure your app sidecar injects the header before any upstream retries — otherwise the span_id will differ between attempts.

Onc e we've validated the end-to-end path and mapping rules, we'll produce a short evidence packet for audit (screenshot + sample event).

Subject: Re: Observability dry-run: edge forwarder -> SIEM ingestion and trace hooks

A couple network clarifications from infra: 

- Egress IPs/Ports: Allow outbound TCP/443 to 34.120.45.9 and 34.120.46.10. If customers are routing through an outbound NAT gateway, please ensure the NAT uses static IPs; ephemeral NATs will break our token allowlist approach.
- Proxy auth: we support Basic auth and NTLM for corporate proxies; when possible prefer an allowlist on the proxy for the HEC token header (x-hec-token) rather than basic auth chaining.
- MTU & keepalive: if the forwarder sits in an enclave with 1400 MTU please set keepalive interval to 30s and tune batch sizes to avoid fragmentation. 

Small operational tip: run the forwarder in a sidecar with minimal privileges and bind it to 127.0.0.1 of the app container; this avoids unexpected host network egress rules.
